main_text.p: habet prolixiorem, quàm ille locus, qui vicinior est æquatori. Vt autem dies in vno loco increscit, ita nox in altero decrescit: & dividitur incrementum hoc in duas partes, ratione anticipationis ortus solaris, & retardationis occasus eius. Ortus enim illius anticipat in loco vno, & retardatur occasus eius, vt simul anticipet collectionem diurnam, & retardet exitum eius: in loco autem altero anticipat collectio nocturna, & retardatur exitus eius. Si sol fuerit in signis meridionalibus, diversum accidet: etenim locus qui propinquus est æquatori, diem habet prolixiorem, quàm habeat alter locus, qui remotior est ab illo: in nocte autem contrarium huius accidit: & dies colligitur primùm, & exit postea in loco propinquiore, vt nox colligatur primùm, & exeat postea in loco remotiore. Anticipatio autem collectionum illarum & retardatio exitus earum vnius est quantitatis: qui enim excessus est vnius loci ab altero, dividitur in duas partes, ratione collectionis & exitus. Si fuerit duorum locorum differentia in latitudine & longitudine, vt sint in duobus circulis æquatori parallelis, habeatq; duos meridianos; illud accidit duobus modis. Vt locus vnus, qui maiorem habet longitudinem, propinquior sit orienti, quàm alter: vel sit remotior, sole peruagante signa septentrionalia: tunc locus ille qui maiorem habet latitudinem, dies habet prolixiores, quàm alter: noctes autem in altero sunt prolixiores. page.notes: Long s is printed as f throughout and is given as s. Several u/v forms are changed to the consonant or vowel spelling required by the rules (diuiditur, diuersum, increfcit, decrefcit). The hyphen at the end of "tranf-" is the printed line-end hyphen; the rest of the word is on the following page. The text has no visible paragraph indents on this page, so it is kept as one paragraph. Some abbreviation marks, such as the one on "habeatq;" and the accent on "quàm", are uncertain and not marked with [?]; the scan is faint in places.
